key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr on DSS 2205 in 1 M H2SO4, a spray distance of 190 mm gave the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance can materially improve coating integrity and acid-corrosion protection for stainless-steel components used in aggressive industrial environments.
method: D-gun spray Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm
Evaluate surface/microstructure with SEM and porosity measurements
Test electrochemical behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization
evidence_signal: The abstract reports porosity decreasing from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, with the 190 mm coating showing the lowest corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate.
watch_item: The optimum distance is specific to this powder/system/substrate/electrolyte condition, so it should be revalidated before transfer to other materials or spray setups.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
